shortcut_name: collapse pulses into a static undirected simple graph
evidence: "adj = [set() for _ in range(n)]" and "common = adj[i] & adj[j]"; "adj[u] |= 1 << (v - 1)"; "find a pair ... that are connected"
affordance_in_statement: Upon receiving this pulse, registry u sets its v-th state bit to 1, and registry v sets its u-th state bit to 1.
removal_suggestion: Change the update rule from setting each bit to 1 to toggling each affected bit. Repeated pulses on the same pair must then be distinguished by parity, while the provided examples remain unchanged because they contain no duplicate pairs.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Stores every pulse as an undirected adjacency-set edge and detects a triangle through common neighbors.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: registry u sets its v-th state bit to 1, and registry v sets its u-th state bit to 1

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Stores the relation as a symmetric bitset graph and checks whether three IDs form three graph edges.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Each pulse is a pair of registry IDs (u, v)

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats the anomaly as an ordinary undirected graph triangle and searches connected neighbor pairs.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: registry u sets its v-th state bit to 1, and registry v sets its u-th state bit to 1

common_affordance: Because updates are idempotent and symmetric, the final state is exactly a static undirected simple graph, so the anomaly is an ordinary triangle.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Enumerates all O(n^3) triples with itertools.combinations, which is too slow for n up to 2000.

recommended_edit: Replace "sets its v-th state bit to 1" and the corresponding reverse update with "toggles its v-th state bit" and "toggles its u-th state bit". This makes duplicate pulses parity-sensitive and invalidates all set- or bitwise-OR-based static-graph solutions.
